mechanism_narrative: The accelerating week-on-week decline in RETAIL_REC (-10.1 to -52.4) reflects a self-reinforcing contraction in discretionary mobility: as fewer people go out, local businesses reduce hours/capacity, further suppressing footfall, so the downward trend persists over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week from -10.1 to -52.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the decline trend reversed rather than persisted.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility crosses above +20 percent change from baseline (as it just did at +21.0), this signals a stay-at-home policy regime is binding tightly on the population, which mechanically suppresses RETAIL_REC for at least the next two weeks as compliance remains high.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stabilizes over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +20, indicating policy binding no longer suppresses retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: Joint collapse of TRANSIT (-20.6 to -55.4) and WORKPLACES (-16.0 to -40.6) indicates both commuting and work-based errand trips are disappearing simultaneously; this compounded reduction in trip-chaining opportunities (e.g., shopping on the way to/from work) drives a steeper additional decline in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall more than 15 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both declined every week in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks is no steeper than a linear extrapolation of its own trend despite continued joint TRANSIT/WORKPLACES declines, rejecting the compounding interaction.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility from its t-2w trough (-19.3) to near-zero by t-0w (-15.6, improving from -2.9 at t-1w to a less negative value) suggests households are substituting retail trips with outdoor recreation during early relaxation of movement restrictions, which only partially substitutes for retail and leaves RETAIL_REC still declining but at a decelerating rate within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -19.3 at t-2w toward -15.6 at t-0w after an intermediate peak at -2.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues declining at the same or faster rate as PARKS mobility recovers, showing no substitution relationship between the two series.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility turning negative for the first time at t-0w (-4.4, after being positive the prior three weeks) signals that even essential-trip mobility is now being suppressed, which indicates the overall mobility floor has not yet been reached and predicts a further one-week drop in RETAIL_REC before any stabilization.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns negative after prior weeks of positive values
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was positive at t-3w,t-2w,t-1w (4.4,0.1,4.6) and turned negative at t-0w (-4.4)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises in the next week even though GROCERY_PHARM remains negative, rejecting the floor-not-reached mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Continued week-on-week declines in WORKPLACES mobility (-16.0 to -40.6) reflect expanding workplace closure policies; since workplace trips often bundle with nearby retail stops, the next week's RETAIL_REC will fall in proportion to the most recent WORKPLACES drop.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined every week from -16.0 to -40.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the next week despite WORKPLACES posting another week-on-week drop of comparable magnitude.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL time (6.7 to 21.0) combined with falling TRANSIT (-20.6 to -55.4) jointly indicate a shift to a fully home-centered lifestyle where both the desire and the means to travel for retail are simultaneously reduced, producing a deeper and more persistent four-week decline in RETAIL_REC than either trend alone would suggest.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 15 points while TRANSIT falls below -40 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 21.0 and TRANSIT reached -55.4 in the same t-0w week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks matches or is shallower than its recent trend despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated and TRANSIT staying depressed, rejecting the compounding behavioral shift.

mechanism_narrative: If local policy carves out exemptions for outdoor recreation (evidenced by PARKS partially recovering from -19.3 to -15.6 while RETAIL_REC keeps falling), warming spring weather combined with outdoor exemptions will continue drawing mobility toward PARKS and away from enclosed retail spaces, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next two weeks even if general restrictions ease.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS mobility diverged positively relative to RETAIL_REC's continued decline over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS move in the same direction over the next two weeks, indicating no substitution effect from outdoor exemption policy.
